title: Bette Davis's birth chart
metaDescription: Bette Davis's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 15.5° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 15.5° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 15.5° Aries — deep enough in the second decan (10°–20°) that the Sun, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 19.5° Pisces, Mars was at 29.0° Taurus. Read together: thought steeped in tone and memory; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Venus to Mars, a conjunction with 0.8° of slack. Two bodies in the same degree are not read as neighbours but as a merger: whatever one wants, the other is already funding. Behind it, the Sun square Uranus at 1.3°, and Jupiter trine Saturn at 1.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Uranus opposes Neptune while both square the Sun. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks four placements here. The Sun in Aries at 15.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Pisces at 19.5° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Taurus at 29.0° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Aries at 2.1° is in fall. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 3 fire, 2 air, 2 water, 2 earth; by modality, 4 cardinal, 3 mutable, 2 fixed. Fire signs carry the scheme’s forward pressure: heat applied early, patience treated as a later skill. Venus crossed from Taurus into Gemini during that day, so its sign is left open. Nothing here ran retrograde — all ten in direct motion that day.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Gemini for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.7° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 12.1°.
